narrative:
INVENTORY OPTIMIZATION ANALYSIS - PL1__M5C259FA

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
This analysis optimizes inventory policy for material PL1__M5C259FA using historical demand and lead time data.
The material exhibits smooth demand patterns (CV=0.216) with unstable lead time 
behavior (CV=0.408). 

KEY FINDINGS:
- Mean daily demand: 1394.22 units/day
- Mean lead time: 4.02 days (ranging from 0.08 to 7.17 days)
- Recommended safety stock: 3888 units (vs SAP: 881 units)
- Optimized order quantity: 10473 units (EOQ-based, constrained by capacity)
- Reorder point: 9495 units
- Review period: 8 days

COST IMPLICATIONS:
The optimized policy results in a total annual cost of $9051.32 compared to the SAP 
baseline of $7165.23. While this represents an increase of $1886.09 
(26.3%), the higher safety stock provides 95.0% service level 
protection against demand and lead time variability, reducing stockout risk significantly.

CAPACITY UTILIZATION:
The policy operates at 100.0% of maximum storage capacity 
(14361/14361 units). MEDIUM: Operating near capacity limit (>90% utilization).

RISK FACTORS:
- Lead time instability (CV=0.408) increases uncertainty in replenishment cycles
- 6 demand outliers detected, indicating occasional demand spikes
- Trend analysis shows slight upward demand trajectory (slope=0.2786 units/day)

RECOMMENDATION:
Implement the optimized policy with close monitoring of lead time performance. Consider supplier development 
initiatives to reduce lead time variability. ATTENTION: Optimized solution increases costs vs SAP baseline. Higher safety stock drives up holding costs.
